text.p: Shares were lower all session on Friday, dragged in late trade to end almost at their lowest as U.S. PPI and retail sales data hit bonds and Wall Street stocks at the open, brokers said. Trade was modest.

The HEX general index fell 1.31 percent to close at 2,811.83 points, but the dividend-adjusted index fell clearly less, down 0.81 percent at 3,183.68. The FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark fell 1.48 percent to 978.86.
On the week, the HEX was down 3.8 percent.
Brokers said the market was largely in the grip of U.S. interest rate hike fears and would lack domestic incentives until Q1 reports start coming late this month.
"It was a very boring market today," one broker said. "Almost the all volume was in-house deals linked to dividends."
Volume was 500 million markka of which Nokia accounted for just over a quarter. Brokers expected trade to remain thin.
Nokia closed down 4.80 markka at 300.00, trading just below the equivalent of 300 in early dealings on Wall Street.
Brokerage Opstock forecast Finnish listed companies' net profits would rise to 23.4 billion markka this year and 29.5 billion in 1998 from 19.9 billion in 1996.
But it noneless recommended a shift to underweight in Q2 from overweight in Q1, due to the overseas rate jitters.
